isolated_target.isolation_note: Fresh VirtualBox VM created from the Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation ISO. No product repo files were present in the guest before installer/package transfer.

steps_completed: Booted a Windows 11 Enterprise Evaluation VM.
Copied the rebuilt v1.3.0 Windows setup executable into the guest.
Installed the NSIS package silently inside the guest.
Started the WSL2 Ubuntu bootstrap from the installer UI.
Approved the Microsoft PowerShell elevation prompt.
Installer enabled Windows WSL components and saved a reboot-required resume state.
Rebooted the VM and reopened the CivicCast Installer.
Reran the WSL2 Ubuntu bootstrap from the installer UI.
Retested the final rebuilt setup executable after WSL bootstrap parser hardening.
Installer displayed an actionable virtualization/IT-help blocker instead of a generic missing-WSL loop.
attempts.blocker_evidence: The Windows guest reports: WSL2 is unable to start since virtualization is not enabled on this machine; error code Wsl/InstallDistro/Service/RegisterDistro/CreateVm/HCS/HCS_E_HYPERV_NOT_INSTALLED. VirtualBox on this host did not expose nested virtualization to the guest, so the WSL2 distro cannot start and the installer-to-dashboard path cannot complete in this VM.
attempts.operator_visible_result: Windows installed WSL components, but this machine does not expose virtualization for WSL2. Turn on virtualization or ask IT for help, then rerun CivicCast Installer.
attempts.repo_commitment: Do not tag or publish v1.3.0 as a public tester release until this lane passes on a nested-virtualization-capable clean Windows target or an equivalent Windows Sandbox/Hyper-V target.

attempts.command: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 --exec bash -lc '<fresh venv install from artifacts/release/v1.3.0/wheelhouse; import civiccast; print(civiccast.__version__)>'
attempts.result: The rebuilt wheelhouse installed in a fresh temporary WSL2 user venv and imported CivicCast 1.3.0.
